I'll think through this as the farmer, then give the plan.

**My thinking:**

Last year went alright so I do mostly the same this year. I have 8.5 mu. Most of it I keep for wheat-maize — that's what everyone in our village does, and two harvests a year is better than one. I'll put 6 mu in wheat-maize rotation. Then 1.5 mu cotton — my wife helps pick and it brings cash. The last 1 mu I plant mungbean after we harvest the wheat on a small corner, it doesn't need much and the family eats some.

For wheat, I buy the improved seed from the dealer in town, same brand neighbor Wang uses, he got over 450 kg last year. I spread about 2 bags of compound fertilizer (diammonium) before sowing, then topdress urea at green-up — works out to around 20 kg nitrogen per mu. Better a little extra than short. I water 4 times — winter water is important, then green-up, jointing, and when grain fills. Spray 2-3 times for aphids and powdery mildew.

Maize I plant right after wheat harvest, no plough — just seed into the stubble, saves diesel. Hybrid seed, one bag does maybe 3 mu. Fertilize at planting and once more when knee-high. Rain does most of the watering in summer, maybe one extra if dry in August.

Cotton needs more work — plough properly, plastic mulch, and I spray many times for bollworm. It's costly but price is okay.

Mungbean is easy, low input, fixes its own nitrogen my father said.
